page.description: FreeBSD editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A complete BSD operating system, not Linux: its own kernel, userland and package tools. The disc1 image installs offline; bootonly fetches the system over the network.
pros: One integrated system: kernel, userland and packages from the same project.
Stable branches with long support; 15.1 is supported to December 2029.
ZFS on the root filesystem in the installer.
The handbook documents the whole system in one place.
cons: Not Linux: Linux-only tools, drivers and instructions do not apply.
The installer is text-based and expects you to make partitioning choices.
Disc1 carries the packages for an offline install; bootonly needs a network.
The Commons screenshot shows FreeBSD 12, not 15.1.
page.previewNote: A stock screenshot of FreeBSD 12 from Wikimedia Commons. It is not 15.1 and not a ROMinit recording: no image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted for this page.

shot.caption: Stock screenshot of FreeBSD 12 · not 15.1, no USB written, no boot tested.

page.status: Two official images: disc1 for an offline install and bootonly for a network install, written with dd or any image writer. Writing erases the stick; the installer then partitions or erases the target disk.

editions.name: Disc1
editions.description: The full installer image with the packages needed for an offline installation.
editions.usbNote: 1.4 GB image: use a stick that fits it. Write it with dd or any image writer; writing erases the stick.

editions.name: Bootonly
editions.description: A small installer that fetches the rest of the system from FreeBSD's mirrors.
editions.usbNote: 550 MB image. Write it with dd or any image writer; writing erases the stick.

editions.name: DVD (dvd1)
editions.description: The installer plus a larger package set on one DVD image.
editions.usbNote: 4.5 GB image. Write it with dd or any image writer; writing erases the stick.
